criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.

Given a CSV/XLSX file with recruiter interactions, when I upload it, then the data is ingested into the system.
Given an invalid file format, when I attempt to upload, then I receive an error message.
Trust: Data ingestion is logged for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Persistence (SQLite via Sequelize) and audit logging added on top of the existing schema/parser/validator work. Ingestion now persists directly (IngestionBatch + RecruiterInteractionRecord) rather than deferring to a normalization stage, since none exists yet and STORY-002 needs the data to survive across requests — documented as a deliberate amendment in directives/vendor_ingestion_stage.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Idempotency dedup key is the uploaded file's SHA-256 hash (translated from CLAUDE.md's vendor_id/source/file_hash convention, which doesn't map to this recruiter-interaction schema). Every outcome (success, duplicate, rejected) writes an IngestionAuditLog row with a per-request correlationId echoed back in the HTTP response. 47/47 backend tests passing; tsc --noEmit clean.

criteria.text: Given a job seeker is logged in, when they navigate to the dashboard, then they see a list of recruiter interactions.
Given a job seeker clicks on a recruiter interaction, when they view the details, then it loads within three clicks.
Trust: Every interaction detail view is logged with a timestamp.

stories.notes: Added the backend's first runnable entry point (backend/src/index.ts) since STORY-001 built the ingestion pipeline but never wired it into an app. Dashboard is server-rendered HTML (GET /dashboard, GET /dashboard/interactions/:id) reading the existing RecruiterInteractionRecord model via a new read-only service (recruiterInteractionsService) — no new frontend toolchain. All interpolated recruiter-supplied fields (name, company, notes) are HTML-escaped; verified live that an injected <script> tag renders inert. Dashboard-to-detail navigation is 1 click, inside the 3-click budget. Every successful detail fetch writes an InteractionViewLog row (interactionId + viewedAt), including repeat views; a 404 writes nothing. Failure paths covered: list/detail service errors render a 500 error page instead of crashing, unknown id renders 404, malformed id renders 400 — all with tests. Known gap, called out and accepted with the user before building: there is no auth system yet in this codebase (no story for one in r0), so 'job seeker is logged in' is satisfied as a single implicit job seeker rather than real login — revisit once an auth story exists. 63/63 backend tests passing; tsc --noEmit clean.

criteria.text: Given a set of recruiter interaction data, when I manually review the data, then I can confirm the data is accurately attributed to the correct recruiter.
Given a data entry with incorrect attribution, when I identify and correct it, then the system updates the attribution correctly.
Trust: Every manual correction is logged with the reviewer ID and timestamp.

stories.notes: Built as a data-reviewer-facing manual review interface, per the story narrative and STORY-000's owner list ('Data Reviewer' owns STORY-003) rather than REQ-004's literal 'job seekers' wording, which appears to be a mismatched requirement -- flagged to the user and confirmed rather than silently building around it; REQ-004's text should be corrected to say 'data reviewer' to match. No auth system exists (same gap as STORY-002's implicit job seeker), so reviewer identity is captured as a required free-text reviewer ID field on the review form itself rather than a login -- deliberately not stubbed with a placeholder, since REQ-007 is a SAFE requirement and a fake ID would make the Trust criterion trivially true. New AttributionReview log records every review action (confirmed or corrected) with reviewerId, previous/new recruiter name+company, and a timestamp; confirming is treated as a real review event and logged too, not just corrections, since a reviewer confirming correct attribution is itself the manual-review action REQ-004/REQ-010 ask for. Attribution update + log write share one transaction. Failure paths covered with tests: missing reviewer ID and empty recruiter name re-render the form with the error and preserve what the reviewer typed rather than losing it, unknown/malformed interaction id, and save failures (mocked service rejection) all leave the underlying record untouched. Verified live end-to-end against an isolated server/database (not reusing the developer's running instance): uploaded data, opened the review form, submitted a correction, confirmed it applied and redirected, and confirmed the missing-reviewer-ID path leaves the record unchanged. 78/78 backend tests passing; tsc --noEmit clean.
